answer: Submissions that land within 145 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The ridge detector writes to quill, and horizon makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 15 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
